plan.contextChunk: This figure is a single Cartesian graph showing a rational function together with the two asymptotes it approaches. The horizontal x-axis carries integer ticks from -5 to 5, the vertical y-axis carries even ticks from -12 to 12, and both are tipped with arrowheads. A dashed orange vertical line stands at x = 1 and runs the full height of the frame, labeled x = 1 in orange near its lower end. A dashed teal line of steep positive slope crosses from the lower left to the upper right, labeled Slant asymptote y = 3x + 1 above and right of the origin. The function is a solid dark blue curve in two branches. The left branch enters at the lower left pressed against the teal line, rises to a shallow turning point just below the x-axis near x = 0, then plunges off the bottom of the frame as it nears the orange line. The right branch descends from the top just right of x = 1, turns at a minimum near y = 9, and climbs away to the upper right, again closing on the teal line. Drawing the curve and both dashed lines on one set of axes lets the reader compare each branch against the boundary it hugs. The graph illustrates the case in which the numerator exceeds the denominator in degree by one, so the polynomial quotient supplies a slanted rather than horizontal end behavior.

demo_steps.title: See the full relationship
demo_steps.narration: In the combined view, the dark blue rational curve is drawn with two dashed asymptotes. The orange line x = 1 controls the break in the graph, while the teal line y = 3x + 1 describes the diagonal end behavior.

demo_steps.title: Approach the vertical asymptote
demo_steps.narration: Drag the probe toward x = 1 from either side. As the horizontal distance to x = 1 shrinks, the function values shoot upward or downward, showing local blow-up near the vertical asymptote.

demo_steps.title: Move toward the ends
demo_steps.narration: Move the probe far left or far right. The point stays close to the dashed teal line, showing that y = 3x + 1 is the boundary that controls end behavior.

demo_steps.title: Separate function from asymptotes
demo_steps.narration: Switch among curve-only, asymptotes-only, and combined views. The asymptotes guide the curve's behavior, but neither dashed line is itself part of the rational function.

interactionPlan.keyInsight: A vertical asymptote describes what happens near a forbidden x-value, while a slant asymptote describes what the rational function looks like as x goes far left or far right.
interactionPlan.reconstructionNotes: Use a single 2D Cartesian graph with a white background and black axes crossing at the origin. Plot the rational curve in dark blue, preferably matching f(x) = 3x + 1 + 2/(x - 1), with a gap at x = 1. Draw the vertical asymptote as a dashed orange line at x = 1 and label it in orange near the bottom. Draw the slant asymptote as a dashed teal line y = 3x + 1 and label it in teal near the middle-right of the graph. The left curve branch should hug the slant line at the lower left, crest slightly below the x-axis, and plunge downward near x = 1. The right branch should enter from above just right of x = 1, dip to a minimum around y = 9, and rise toward the upper right while tracking the slant line. In curve-only mode hide both dashed asymptotes and labels; in asymptotes-only mode hide the blue curve; in combined mode show all. The probe should avoid plotting exactly at x = 1 and may display an undefined warning or snap to the nearest valid side if the slider lands on the asymptote.

authoredContext:
To find the equation of the slant asymptote, divide 3 x 2 −2x+1 x−1. The quotient is 3x+1, and the remainder is 2. The slant asymptote is the graph of the line g(x)=3x+1. See the figure.

Slant Asymptote when f(x)= p(x) q(x),q(x)≠0 where degree of p>degree of qby1.

Graph of f(x)=(3x^2-2x+1)/(x-1) with its vertical asymptote at x=1 and a slant asymptote aty=3x+1.

Case 3: If the degree of the denominator = degree of the numerator, there is a horizontal asymptote at y= a n b n, where a n and b n are the leading coefficients of p(x) and q(x) for f(x)= p(x) q(x),q(x)≠0.
